question.text: Why was Section 18A inserted into the Securities Contracts (Regulation) Act specifically for derivative contracts?

answer.text: To give legal validity to derivative contracts that are traded on recognized stock exchanges and settled through the clearing house of the exchange under its rules and bye-laws
To impose a special tax on derivative transactions conducted on recognized exchanges
To mandate that all derivative contracts must be physically settled through delivery of the underlying asset
To prohibit foreign investors from participating in Indian derivative markets

explanation.text: The Logic: Section 18A of the SCRA provides that derivative contracts are legal and valid if they are traded on a recognized stock exchange and settled on the clearing house of the recognized stock exchange in accordance with its rules and bye-laws. This anchors exchange-traded derivatives in the SCRA framework. The Trap: Section 18A is about legal validity of exchange-traded derivative contracts — it is not a tax measure, a settlement-mode mandate, or a participant restriction. Note: The protection is tied to trading on a recognized stock exchange and clearing through its clearing house, not to any specific contract type.
